messages:
Alex: Quick thread — proposal to simplify the prefix handshake state machine. current flow (lease -> prefill -> pin -> serve) has too many transient states and causes subtle eviction/read races when demote happens during apply.
Maya: tl;dr: fewer states, stronger invariants. can you sketch the new flow?
Alex: idea: collapse `lease` + `pin` into a single `claim` with 3 outcomes: CLAIMED, STALE, FAILED. on CLAIMED you may serve; on STALE you trigger a re-fetch; FAILED = fallback to remote. removes the mid-state where something is "pinned but not yet resident".
Liam: sounds promising. how do we handle concurrent demote + write? that was the biggest correctness pain.
Alex: keep demote idempotent and introduce a small sequencer token per claim. sequence ensures demote with older token is ignored. simpler than full epoch CAS.
Sophia: so token is monotonic per prefix handoff. if a write arrives with token T and demote with T-1 happens, demote no-op because token mismatch. is that the invariant?
Alex: exactly. invariant: only demote actions with token >= current_token are applied. claim increments token on successful claim.
Evan: what's the fallback ordering for reads when claim fails or is stale? current feels ad-hoc and causes extra remote trips.
Alex: propose deterministic fallback ordering: 1) if local residency present -> serve. 2) if claim in-flight -> wait up to W ms (config). 3) if claim returns STALE -> try local secondary shard (fast remap) for hot tenants. 4) finally, fallback to remote store/model. keeps most paths local-first and avoids thundering remote calls.
Maya: W ms needs to be tuned per route. for embeddings we can use smaller W than generation prep. add per-route override config.
Liam: telemetry: we need metrics for claim.latency, claim.outcome (CLAIMED/STALE/FAILED), fallback.counts per reason, and demote.token_mismatch_count. will help tune W.
Sophia: rollout plan? big refactors here risk subtle regressions.
Alex: feature-flagged rollout: handshake_simplify=v1. smoke tests: small canary in dedicated pool, route pinned tenants only. if metrics are good after 4 hours -> 10% -> 50% -> full. include automated regression: read-after-write smoke that does write+read loop under concurrent demote for 30s.
Evan: can you paste the smoke script we can run in CI?
Alex: sure

```
# smoke.sh (pseudo)
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -X POST /kv/write -d '{"prefix":"p","k":"k","v":"v$RANDOM"}'
  curl -s -X GET "/kv/read?p=p&k=k" | grep "v" || echo "read-miss $i"
done
```

Alex: run that while running the demote stress harness: `./tools/demote_stress --prefix p --rate 200/s`.
Maya: tests: add a unit for token comparison and an integration that injects old-token demotes to ensure no data loss.
Liam: implementation note: simplify in-memory state machine transition table down to 4 handlers. reduces code paths and makes formal reasoning easier.
Sophia: any perf regression risk? collapsing states might increase lock hold time.
Alex: good call — we must keep the claim path non-blocking. use an atomic token bump + optimistic prefill. only acquire short-term lock for residency map update.
Evan: I worry about multi-tenant fairness — if we wait W ms for claim in-flight, hot tenants could block others.
Alex: add per-tenant concurrency budget and an admission policy: if budget exhausted, don't wait, fall back immediately. this avoids head-of-line blocking.
Maya: agree. also expose metrics: wait_suppressed_count.
cache-bot: alert: new metric proposal registered: `handshake.claim_outcome`, `handshake.fallback_reason`, `handshake.demote_mismatch`
Liam: final ask: put an RFC PR describing token semantics, fallback ordering table, and the exact metric names. I'll review before dev picks it up.
Alex: will draft RFC tonight. thanks all — if no objections I'll open the feature-flagged patch w/ smoke tests tomorrow. :thumbsup:
